page: Microsoft Azure E32a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EAv4 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instructions.

This server includes 819 GB of local SSD storage. In benchmark evaluations, the E32a_v4 demonstrates average performance across most workloads. Its multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, and multi-core Geekbench scores fall within the middle 50% of tested servers. However, single-core CPU performance in stress-ng is poor, placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is stable, with read-only large block speeds at 112.96 GB/sec and write speeds at 57.02 GB/sec. It shows strong performance in image processing and small-model LLM text generation, both ranking in the top 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E32a_v4 offers a dense memory configuration relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require top-tier single-core CPU performance. The inclusion of 819 GB of local SSD storage provides fast local scratch space without requiring external storage attachments. This server is best suited for memory-intensive applications such as relational databases, caching layers like Redis, data processing pipelines, and medium-scale web serving.
